title: Mount Elbrus Expedition: Summit of Europe
overview: An expedition to the summit of Mount Elbrus in the Caucasus — the highest peak in Europe at 5,642 m. The climb is based at the Gara-Bashi high camp, with acclimatisation hikes to Mount Cheget and Pastukhov Rocks before a night summit push.
A reserve day is built in for weather. Accommodation, meals, permits, the cable car and a professional support team are included.

itinerary.title: Arrival at Mineralnye Vody → Terskol/Cheget (2,100 m)
itinerary.subtitle: 180 km · 3–4 hours by road

activities.title: Meet the team at MRV airport

itinerary.title: Acclimatisation hike to Pastukhov Rocks (4,800 m)
itinerary.subtitle: 6 km · 5–6 hours round trip

activities.title: Summit push begins
activities.text: Around 22:00–23:00 on foot, or 01:00–02:00 by snowcat, depending on conditions.

activities.title: Gara-Bashi → Pastukhov Rocks
activities.text: 4 km, 3–4 hours on foot or about 1 hour by snowcat.

activities.title: Summit attempt if needed
activities.text: Otherwise descend to Terskol/Cheget and celebrate.

inclusions: Meals from Day 1 dinner to Day 8 breakfast
Cable car to Gara-Bashi and back
exclusions: Flights to and from Mineralnye Vody
Costs from changes beyond our control

good_to_know.title: Fitness
good_to_know.text: Good cardiovascular fitness is essential. Start a training plan of walking, stair climbs and cardio at least 8–12 weeks before departure.

good_to_know.title: Gear
good_to_know.text: A detailed gear list is shared on booking. Personal trekking and mountaineering gear can be rented on request.

good_to_know.title: Altitude
good_to_know.text: The itinerary includes acclimatisation days. Guides monitor every trekker and the plan may change for safety.

good_to_know.title: Documents
good_to_know.text: A valid passport, visa where required, and medical and evacuation insurance details are needed before travel.

faqs.question: Where does the expedition start and end?
faqs.answer: The expedition starts and ends at Mineralnye Vody (MRV) airport. Flights are not included.

faqs.question: Do I need prior trekking experience?
faqs.answer: Prior multi-day trekking experience is recommended. Our team will talk you through fitness preparation before you book.

faqs.question: What happens if the weather turns?
faqs.answer: Buffer and reserve days are built in. Final decisions on summit attempts are made by the expedition leaders for everyone’s safety.

faqs.question: Who leads the expedition?
faqs.answer: Adventure journeys are run with Anmish Adventures, led by mountaineer Anmish Varma, with experienced local guides and support staff.
